headline: Sonny Gray returns to shut down Detroit as the Red Sox finish the sweep
morning_brew: Wednesday night in Detroit was exactly what we needed to see from this rotation. Sonny Gray looked like his old self in his return from injury, tossing five scoreless innings and giving up only four hits. I been sayin' it all year, this rotation needs a horse, and he finally looked like one out there on the bump. The bullpen followed up with four innings of no-hit ball to secure the four to zero victory. Finishing a sweep on the road gives this squad a little bit of life before the Rays come to the Fens tonight.

Jaylen Brown is making headlines today after saying he could see himself in green for the next ten years. It is nice to hear some loyalty after the way this season ended, but talk is cheap in the offseason. Brad Stevens is already out there doing damage control, saying Jaylen has not expressed any frustration to him directly. We expect greatness in this town, and another summer of speculation is the last thing anyone wants to deal with right now. I'll believe the commitment when I see another trophy.

Down in Foxborough, Drake Maye is already acting like a leader by backing his head coach. He told reporters he is not worried about Mike Vrabel's off-field issues being a distraction this season. It is a tough spot for a young quarterback to be in, but the kid seems to have a good head on his shoulders. We are looking at a roster with some glaring holes even after the draft, and we need everyone focused if we are going to improve on last year's record. Let the league handle the process, we just need to see progress on the field.

trend_watch.dans_take: He is the anchor of this rotation and we need him healthy to have any prayer in the East.

trend_watch.dans_take: Rough night at the dish for Wilyer, but a win is a win.
